evaluationApproach.summary: Evaluate dependable practical support during training and weekend games: reliability, player supervision, communication, safety, collaboration and respect for the lead coach's direction. Do not require advanced tactical analysis or independent Head Coach responsibilities.
evaluationApproach.corePrinciple: A strong Amateur Assistant Coach makes sessions and match days safer and more organized within the authority assigned by the club and lead coach.

mandatoryRules.rule: Score this amateur support position only; do not apply professional Assistant Coach, Head Coach or office staff standards.
Do not require scouting, a game model, independent session planning or advanced tactical analysis.
Reward safe supervision, practical reliability, appropriate escalation and constructive player communication.
Do not assume verified licenses, transport authorization, background checks or safeguarding clearance.
Do not score accent, grammar, appearance, identity or video production quality.
Treat written/video contradictions as matters for review, not automatic proof of dishonesty.

calibrationOverall.strongestAreas: Training setup and support; age-appropriate communication; positive player guidance; practical reliability
calibrationOverall.mainWeaknesses: Limited detailed examples of handling difficult match-day situations; limited evidence of follow-up and verified experience
calibrationOverall.summary: The score describes the fictional answers supplied, not a verified candidate or an automatic hiring decision. Safeguarding clearance, references, permissions and club requirements require separate verification.

questions.text: Tell us about your soccer, coaching, or youth-development experience.
strong: Identifies specific soccer, coaching, education, volunteering or youth-work experience.
Explains actual responsibilities, age groups and environments.
Connects prior experience to supporting coaches and players.
questions.acceptable: Provides some relevant experience but limited detail about responsibilities or application.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Relies only on being a soccer fan or player, exaggerates experience, or gives no connection to the role.

calibration.response: I volunteered with a U12 team last season, helped set up drills, checked attendance and supported players during small-group work.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: Why do you want to work as an assistant coach in an amateur club or academy?
questions.evaluates: Motivation, commitment and understanding of the amateur environment.
strong: Shows genuine interest in helping players and coaches.
Recognizes the practical and service-oriented nature of the role.
Demonstrates realistic availability and willingness to learn.
questions.acceptable: Shows positive motivation but gives generic reasons or limited evidence of commitment.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Focuses only on status, rapid promotion or personal authority and shows little interest in practical support.

calibration.response: I enjoy helping young players improve and want to support the coaches each week while learning more about coaching.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: What do you believe are the main responsibilities of an assistant coach at this level?
strong: Mentions session setup, player supervision, exercise support, positive communication and match-day organization.
Understands that the lead coach sets the main direction.
Recognizes safety, reliability and possible support across several teams.
questions.acceptable: Identifies helping the coach and players but omits some practical or safety responsibilities.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Describes a professional first-team tactical assistant, expects independent authority, or sees practical tasks as beneath the role.

calibration.response: I would prepare equipment, help supervise players and support the coach at practice and games.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: The answer identifies the core responsibility but lacks a specific process, boundary or follow-up.

questions.text: How would you help prepare the field, equipment, and players before a training session?
strong: Arrives early and checks the session plan with the coach.
Sets up safe equipment and playing areas accurately.
Helps with attendance, player readiness and an orderly start.
questions.acceptable: Mentions equipment setup and helping players but provides limited sequence or safety detail.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Waits passively for every instruction, ignores safety checks, or cannot describe basic preparation.

calibration.response: I would arrive early, confirm the session layout, inspect the space for hazards, set out cones and goals, and welcome players.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you support the coach while a training exercise is taking place?
strong: Understands the exercise objective and assigned role.
Observes engagement and safety, manages balls or transitions, and reinforces agreed coaching points.
Communicates observations at an appropriate time without interrupting or contradicting the coach.
questions.acceptable: Provides active support and encouragement but gives limited detail about timing or alignment.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Takes over without permission, gives conflicting instructions, remains disengaged, or humiliates players.

calibration.response: I would check the objective with the coach, keep players engaged, retrieve balls and reinforce the coach's agreed coaching points.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: If the coach asks you to supervise a small group or basic exercise, how would you organize it?
questions.evaluates: Basic delivery, clarity and group management.
strong: Confirms the objective, rules, duration and safety requirements.
Explains and demonstrates simply, checks understanding and keeps players active.
Observes, encourages and gives corrections consistent with the coach's direction.
questions.acceptable: Can organize and explain a basic activity but provides limited detail about checking understanding or adapting it.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Changes the purpose without agreement, cannot control the group, or prioritizes complexity over safe, clear delivery.

calibration.response: I would explain the rules, demonstrate briefly, divide the group safely and check that everyone understands before starting.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you explain an exercise to players who do not understand the coach's instructions?
strong: Uses simple language, a brief demonstration and one or two key points.
Checks understanding through questions or practice.
Adapts explanation without criticizing the player or undermining the coach.
questions.acceptable: Repeats or demonstrates the instruction positively but has a limited method for checking understanding.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Blames the player, raises pressure unnecessarily, gives conflicting information or continues without checking comprehension.

calibration.response: I would simplify the instructions, show the action once and ask a player to demonstrate it back to me.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you encourage a player who is struggling or losing confidence?
strong: Listens and identifies the immediate difficulty.
Uses specific, realistic encouragement and focuses on controllable actions or small progress.
Keeps the player included and informs the coach when further support is needed.
questions.acceptable: Offers positive encouragement and patience but gives generic feedback.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Shames, compares or threatens the player, promises outcomes, or dismisses distress and possible safeguarding concerns.

calibration.response: I would listen to what is difficult, encourage one achievable improvement and keep the player involved in the exercise.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you correct a player while remaining positive and respecting the lead coach's instructions?
strong: Reinforces the coach's terminology and objective.
Gives one clear, actionable correction and recognizes what the player did well.
Chooses appropriate timing and checks whether the correction helped.
questions.acceptable: Provides respectful correction aligned with the exercise but gives limited detail about timing or follow-up.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Publicly criticizes the player, overwhelms them with corrections, or contradicts the coach.

calibration.response: I would praise what the player did well, give one correction using the coach's terminology and check it during the next repetition.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you help the team before, during, and after a weekend game?
strong: Describes timely arrival, equipment and player readiness before kickoff.
Supports warm-up, bench organization, substitutions, observation and calm communication as assigned.
Helps with equipment, player welfare and a professional departure after the game.
questions.acceptable: Identifies several relevant match-day tasks but lacks a complete or organized process.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Focuses mainly on tactical authority, ignores practical responsibilities, or behaves emotionally toward officials, opponents or players.

calibration.response: I would arrive early, help with equipment and warm-ups, organize the bench as directed and clean up after the game.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: What would you do if a player became frustrated about playing time or their position?
questions.evaluates: Emotional judgment, listening and respect for decision authority.
strong: Listens privately and calmly without promising selection or agreeing against the coach.
Acknowledges feelings, reinforces appropriate behavior and directs role decisions to the lead coach.
Escalates concerning conduct or welfare issues appropriately.
questions.acceptable: Responds calmly and refers the matter to the coach but provides limited detail about boundaries or follow-up.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Promises playing time, criticizes the coach, argues publicly, dismisses the player or uses punishment outside assigned authority.

calibration.response: I would listen calmly, tell the player to keep working and refer playing-time decisions to the head coach.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: The answer identifies the core responsibility but lacks a specific process, boundary or follow-up.

questions.text: How would you respond if the coach were temporarily occupied and the players needed supervision?
strong: Keeps players together, safe and engaged in an approved low-risk activity.
Uses known routines and avoids introducing unauthorized tactical or physical work.
Contacts the coach or responsible club official and follows emergency procedures if necessary.
questions.acceptable: Maintains order and safety while waiting for direction but provides limited procedural detail.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Leaves players unsupervised, invents risky activities, exceeds authority or fails to seek responsible support.

calibration.response: I would keep players together and engaged in a safe familiar activity until the coach is available again.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: The answer identifies the core responsibility but lacks a specific process, boundary or follow-up.

questions.text: How would you communicate with the coach if you disagreed with an instruction or decision?
questions.evaluates: Professional disagreement and respect for roles.
strong: Chooses a private and appropriate time.
Asks clarifying questions, explains the concern respectfully and focuses on player or team needs.
Accepts the final decision unless it presents a safety, safeguarding or legal concern that requires escalation.
questions.acceptable: Discusses disagreement privately and respectfully but gives limited detail about escalation or resolution.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Challenges the coach publicly, undermines instructions with players, stays silent about genuine safety concerns or becomes confrontational.

calibration.response: I would discuss my concern privately with the coach after the session and respect the decision unless safety is at risk.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: What would you do if you observed an injury, bullying, unsafe conduct, or a safeguarding concern?
questions.evaluates: Immediate safety awareness and reporting judgment.
strong: Stops or reduces immediate danger within their role and obtains appropriate help.
Follows club emergency, injury and safeguarding procedures and reports to the designated responsible person.
Records facts accurately, preserves privacy and does not investigate or promise secrecy independently.
questions.acceptable: Recognizes the need to protect the player and inform the appropriate coach or club official but lacks procedural detail.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Ignores or minimizes the concern, diagnoses or treats beyond competence, promises secrecy, confronts alleged parties recklessly or posts/discusses it publicly.

calibration.response: I would stop an unsafe activity, seek the designated club contact and follow the reporting procedure rather than investigate myself.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: Amateur clubs often need help with equipment, attendance, field setup, substitutions, transportation coordination, and communication. Which responsibilities can you support, and how would you remain reliable throughout the season?
strong: Identifies realistic duties and distinguishes tasks requiring authorization.
Explains punctuality, scheduling, early communication about conflicts and follow-through.
Shows willingness to help one or several teams while maintaining accurate attendance and safe information handling.
questions.acceptable: Can support several practical tasks and commits to communication, but provides limited detail about reliability systems or boundaries.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Rejects normal support duties, overcommits without a plan, handles transport or personal data casually, or has no process for absences and schedule conflicts.

calibration.response: I can handle equipment, attendance and substitutions as assigned. I use a calendar and tell the coach early if a conflict arises.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: The response is relevant and practical, but would be stronger with a concrete example, verification or measurable follow-through.

questions.text: How would you help integrate a new or shy player into training and the team?
strong: Welcomes the player and explains routines clearly without singling them out.
Pairs the player appropriately and checks understanding and comfort.
Updates the lead coach on relevant support needs while protecting privacy.
questions.acceptable: Provides encouragement and introduction but limited follow-up.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Ignores exclusion, labels the player or shares private information inappropriately.

calibration.response: I would introduce the player, pair them with a supportive teammate and check after the drill how they felt.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Shows an inclusive practical approach; coordination with the lead coach could be clearer.

questions.text: How would you manage a last-minute absence or schedule conflict before a practice or match?
strong: Informs the lead coach as soon as a conflict is known.
Confirms coverage and transfers essential equipment or attendance information securely.
Avoids making promises or leaving children without authorized supervision.
questions.acceptable: Communicates promptly but lacks a practical handover plan.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Fails to notify the club, leaves players unsupervised or shares private details carelessly.

calibration.response: I would call the coach immediately, explain what I can still cover and help arrange an approved replacement.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Prompt and responsible communication; the answer lacks a concrete handover checklist.

questions.text: How would you improve your contribution as an amateur assistant coach during the season?
strong: Asks the lead coach for specific feedback and clarifies expectations.
Reflects on player support, organization and safety after sessions.
Sets achievable improvements and follows through without overstepping the role.
questions.acceptable: Shows willingness to learn but gives no review routine.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Rejects feedback or seeks to override the lead coach.

calibration.response: I would ask for feedback monthly and keep notes on what I can do better at setup and supporting drills.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Shows willingness to improve; the answer does not explain how progress will be measured.
